intro: Gas plant operators monitor complex systems and control equipment where mistakes are costly. The closest of the 25 careers below is Gas Compressor and Gas Pumping Station Operators, with a 90% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $77,320, which is 12% less than the $87,820 gas plant operators earn.
why_it_works: A shift means watching gauges, adjusting flows and acting quickly when readings drift. O*NET rates operations monitoring at 4.12 out of 5 for this job and operation and control at 3.75. Pipeline, rail, nuclear and marine engine jobs use the same control-room discipline. Because your pay is already high, few matches pay more. The skills to add are maintaining, choosing and installing equipment.
tips: Nuclear Technicians earn $110,240, which is 26% more, after a certificate or associate program.
List the control systems and safety programs you know; they transfer directly to other plants.
If you want to move, compare union contracts and shift patterns, which differ a lot between plants.

faq.q: What jobs can former gas plant operators do?
faq.a: The closest matches are gas compressor and pumping station operators (90%), Wellhead Pumpers (80%) and pump operators (78%), based on O*NET 31.0. Locomotive Engineers are also 78% matched and earn $81,410, which is 7% less than the $87,820 gas plant operator median.

faq.q: Which careers for gas plant operators pay more?
faq.a: 5 of the 25 matches pay more. Commercial Pilots earn $123,220 (40% more), Nuclear Technicians $110,240 (26% more) and Ship Engineers $109,530 (25% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Pilot and nuclear roles usually need a certificate or associate degree first.

faq.q: Do gas plant operators need more education to switch?
faq.a: Sometimes. 14 of the 25 matches need no more education than gas plant operators already have, including 8 of the top 10. In the closest match, 65% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and training is mostly on the job.

faq.q: What skills should gas plant operators learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are equipment maintenance, equipment selection, installation and operation and control. Quality control analysis already rates 3.25 out of 5 for your job in O*NET, so hands-on maintenance work is the main step toward better-paid technical roles.
